title: Jethro's advice (Exodus 18)
hookLine: Moses' father-in-law tells him he can't judge everyone alone

lines: THE ONE WHO DOES IT ALL.
A LINE FROM MORNING TO EVENING.
cards: At some workplaces there's one person who answers every question, signs off on every decision, stays late every night, and is quietly falling apart. Or the parent who does all of it because it's faster than explaining.
In the wilderness, Moses is that person. From morning until evening, a line of people stands in front of him, waiting for him to settle their arguments.
Then his father-in-law comes to visit, watches for one day, and says something very plain.

teach.h: A PRIEST OF MIDIAN COMES TO VISIT.
teach.b: Jethro, Yitro in Hebrew, is a priest of Midian, not an Israelite. Moses married his daughter Zipporah years before, when he ran away from Egypt. Now Jethro hears everything God did for the people.

He comes out to the desert, brings Moses's wife and sons, and rejoices with him. The next morning he watches Moses work, and asks: why are you sitting alone, with everyone standing around you from morning to evening?
Moses says, they come to me to ask of God, and I judge between them. Jethro answers, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "The thing that thou doest is not good."

teach.h: THE THING IS TOO HEAVY FOR THEE.
teach.b: You'll wear yourself out, you and the people with you, "for the thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone." Then he gives him a plan. Teach everyone the laws, so they know the way.
Find capable people who fear God, love truth and hate a bribe.
Put them in charge of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens. Let them handle the small cases, and bring you only the hard ones.
And Moses, the man who spoke with God at the burning bush, listens to his father-in-law and does all of it.

teach.h: A PORTION NAMED FOR AN OUTSIDER.
teach.b: A detail the tradition keeps: the Torah portion that holds the Ten Commandments is named Yitro, after an outsider. Good advice, it suggests, can come from outside the camp.

teach.h: THOU ART NOT ABLE TO PERFORM IT ALONE.
teach.b: A whole system of judges began with someone saying, gently, you can't do this alone.

how: Parashat Yitro, which includes Jethro's visit and the Ten Commandments, is read in synagogue each winter as part of the yearly Torah cycle.

o: lead alone, so the people trust one voice
build an altar before every hard decision
share the load: judges for the small cases

games.q: what's inside the advice — tap the pairs.

s: he was a priest of Midian, Moses's father-in-law, from outside the people.
a whole Torah portion is named after Jethro
Parashat Yitro, and it contains the Ten Commandments.
he listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.

games.q: you're Moses. you've led the people out of Egypt. your father-in-law says you're doing it all wrong. what do you do?
o: thank him and change how you work.
explain that God chose you, not him.
games.why: Moses listens and does all that Jethro says. the man of the burning bush takes advice from an outsider.

practice: Picture the line of things waiting for you this week, the way Moses saw a line of people, and walk down it slowly.
Find one thing someone else could do, maybe not your way or as fast, but well enough: a colleague, a partner, a child, a friend, a service.
Picture asking, picture them saying yes, and notice how your shoulders feel when it's off them.

wordCard.voice: Jethro's advice. A father-in-law from Midian tells Moses the work is too heavy for one person, and helps him share it.

orig.note: Hebrew: Jethro. a midrash, quoted by Rashi, links the name to yeter, more.

carryVoice: Your line: you can't carry it alone. Even Moses needed help. See you at the mountain.

sources.q: The thing that thou doest is not good.
for the thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.

sources.ref: Rashi on Exodus 18:13 (debate on the timing of Jethro's visit)
